knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A discharge route is confirmed in writing with the client, the council and the water authority before any water moves. Draining to stormwater without a route is not allowed in this draft.
Releasing fish into NSW public waters needs a fish stocking permit, and dumping an unwanted fish is an offence. The correct response refuses and refers the client to the state rules.
Each unneeded change adds cost and stress and can disturb the tank. Routine changes follow the plan, and extra changes are made only where the results or the plan show a need.

practicalCriteria: Learner runs a bucket test on a training tank, and records the weather, the start and finish times, the levels and the result
Learner refuses a stormwater discharge request in a role-play, and records the route check and the refusal
Learner records the volume, the reason and the approval for a planned routine water change on a training tank
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark. With three questions, all three must be correct. Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation and is not verified by this quiz.
evidenceRequired: Bucket test record with weather, times, levels and result
Water change record with volume, temperature match and reason
Refusal and route-check record for the discharge request
Assessor observation of the bucket test
stopWorkCriteria: Discharge of tank water, sand or sludge to stormwater or a waterway without a confirmed route
Release, sale or donation of any animal, or movement of live rock or plants without the state rules checked
New water added at a temperature or salinity that differs from the tank without a plan
